results.summary: This design lights up a number on a seven-segment display when a switch is pressed. The documentation is very thin, stating only that pressing the right switch should light the right number, and the pin names are generic inputs and outputs. It requires an external seven-segment display and switches, but no wiring details are given. The project appears to be a beginner exercise and provides no test procedure or implementation detail.

This project implements a simple counter built from flip-flops that increments when a pushbutton is pressed and shows the count on a seven-segment display. It is tested by checking that the output counts downward from F to 0, and it is intended to drive an external seven-segment display. The design is a basic educational arithmetic circuit with no further implementation details or silicon results. It is a small personal experiment rather than a complete application.

This project is a 4-bit down counter that counts backward in binary from 1111 (decimal 15) down to 0000 (decimal 0). Every time a clock pulse arrives, the counter subtracts one from its current value. It is tested by checking that the output counts downward from F to 0, and it is intended to drive an external seven-segment display. The design is a basic educational arithmetic circuit with no further implementation details or silicon results.
